final_answer:
Cause: the page cursor stored only created_at and the store paged with `created_at > cursor`. When several events shared a timestamp across a page boundary, the next page skipped the remaining ones, so export_all returned fewer events.

Fix: the feed order is now the unique key (created_at, id). The cursor encodes both fields (cursor.encode/decode, decode now returns a tuple), and EventStore.page sorts by and filters on that tuple. Malformed tokens still raise InvalidCursor. All 7 tests pass. I did not add a regression test for the shared-timestamp case beyond the existing test_shared_timestamp_across_a_page_boundary, which already covers it.
